title: SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 Weighting More Than Doubles as Quarterly Rebalance Trades Execute
detail: Index funds tracking the Nasdaq-100 executed quarterly rebalancing trades at the Sept 18, 2026 close, lifting SpaceX's (SPCX) index weighting to roughly 2.82% from about 1.28% — a boost Wall Street estimated would force $15.5-22 billion in net passive buying, including from the $481B Invesco QQQ Trust. The increase reflects SpaceX's expanding public float as successive post-IPO lock-up tranches expired through August and September. The new weighting takes effect at Monday Sept 21's market open.

media.caption: SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 weighting rises as post-IPO lockups expand its public float

title: NASA Awards SpaceX $946M Contract Modification for Crew-15, Crew-16, Crew-17
detail: NASA announced September 18, 2026 a $946 million firm fixed-price modification to SpaceX's Commercial Crew Transportation Capability (CCtCap) contract, adding three more ISS crew rotation missions — Crew-15, Crew-16 and Crew-17 — with mission readiness dates in 2027 and 2028 and a performance period running through 2030. The award covers ground operations, launch, in-orbit support, return and recovery, cargo transport, and lifeboat capability while Dragon is docked at the station. It brings SpaceX's total CCtCap contract value to $5.92 billion across 17 flights and raises SpaceX's crew-mission count to 17. The modification fills three of six additional post-certification crew missions NASA flagged in a May 2026 notice of intent; the remaining three slots stay open for Boeing's Starliner if it achieves certification — Starliner has yet to complete an operational crew rotation mission after its 2024 crewed test-flight astronauts returned to Earth on Crew Dragon instead.

media.caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 launches a Crew Dragon on a NASA Commercial Crew mission; NASA added three more crew flights (Crew-15/16/17) to the CCtCap contract
